items.raw_snippet: # When every M&A team deploys AI, what’s your competitive advantage? Use AI to challenge and improve decisions, not just to automate processes. *The day before the upcoming board presentation, someone on the team prompted several frontier AI models with a straightforward request: assume this deal fails in two years and tell us the major reasons why. It is increasingly how savvy deal teams use artificial intelligence, not just to accelerate the process, but to pressure-test their underlying investment thesis. From scanning the market for potential targets to synthesizing hundreds of documents in a data room, AI-enabled tools are increasingly embedded across the entire transaction lifecycle. The value is in how your team uses it to make informed decisions. As AI commoditizes analysis, advantage comes from humans focusing on the activities AI can’t automate: creating and approving the deal thesis, building relationships and redesigning workflows to compound learning over time.

They chase these logos not because the deals are big, but because a marquee name on a sales deck supposedly makes every deal after it easier. AI is new, so founders assume they have to educate the market, and they default to the **Lighthouse** strategy: win a few marquee customers, build social proof, and reassure the buyer who’s afraid of making the wrong call. There are two GTM playbooks for AI companies selling into the enterprise: the **Lighthouse** and the **Landgrab**. It’s about what you’re selling and who you’re selling to. items.snippet: # Adoption of artificial intelligence outpaces training in field epidemiology pr...
items.raw_snippet: # Adoption of artificial intelligence outpaces training in field epidemiology programs, new survey finds. A new study found that two-thirds of epidemiologists in specialized training programs used artificial intelligence (AI) in their work, despite only one in five having received AI training and one-quarter expressing ethical concerns about accuracy and bias. For the study, published in *Eurosurveillance*, researchers led by a team at the Public Health Agency of Canada surveyed 105 participants in Field Epidemiology Training Programs (FETPs), referred to as field epidemiologists, about their use of AI. While AI has the potential to improve efficiency for field epidemiologists, the researchers write, it also raises concerns about the development of critical-thinking skills and professional discernment in a field that “places a premium on judgment and interpretation, and the ability to communicate uncertainty.”. Among the 105 respondents, 66% said they use AI in their field epidemiology work.

"We’re now, like, in the singularity," Altman said in an episode of a podcast called "Relentless," which came out on Saturday. The technology seized on Hugging Face as a potential source of models and data sets necessary to complete the test, OpenAI said. items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman heads to Washington as AI policy deadline nears
items.snippet: ## STATE POLITICS & POLICY. Altman will preview his company’s newest model and i...
items.raw_snippet: ## STATE POLITICS & POLICY. Altman will preview his company’s newest model and is likely to face questions about OpenAI’s recent cybersecurity breach. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is expected to return to Washington on Wednesday and Thursday for meetings with the White House and other administration officials as well as bipartisan members of Congress to discuss artificial intelligence policy, according to three people close to the industry and the administration, granted anonymity to detail the meetings. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google jointly submitted extensive “redline” edits to a draft framework from the White House’s Office of the National Cyber Director earlier last week, according to one of the people, who is close to the administration. The administration also stepped in to request OpenAI amend the rollout of its ChatGPT-5.6 model to only government-approved partners, which Altman at the time said was not the company’s “preferred” way of releasing the model and ideally would be alleviated by implementing a more “sustainable” government process to guide companies.

items.title: Sam Altman to meet with Trump administration, senators ...
items.snippet: * He will preview the capabilities of the company's upcoming AI models and field...
items.raw_snippet: * He will preview the capabilities of the company's upcoming AI models and field questions about cybersecurity and the company's stance on open-weight models, according to a source. * The visit lands during a particularly sensitive moment for AI development in the U.S., as a debate over whether to restrict Chinese open-weight AI models rages. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will meet with senior Trump administration officials, lawmakers and economists in Washington, D.C., this week to preview the capabilities of the company's upcoming family of artificial intelligence models, CNBC has learned. This visit lands during a particularly sensitive moment for AI development in the U.S., as a debate over whether to restrict Chinese open-weight AI models has ripped through Silicon Valley in recent weeks. In addition to previewing OpenAI's upcoming releases, Altman is expected to field questions from policymakers about cybersecurity and the company's stance on open-weight models, according to a source familiar with the plans who asked not to be named because the details are confidential.
